question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s extensive consolidation of authority within the Chinese Communist Party and People’s Liberation Army underpins traders’ strong consensus against his removal before 2027. Ongoing high-level purges through 2025 and 2026 have eliminated senior military and political figures, leaving minimal visible opposition or alternative power centers ahead of the 21st Party Congress. At age 73, Xi has shown no public signals of stepping down or designating a successor, instead prioritizing loyalty enforcement and structural control that historically favors extended tenure. While the 2027 congress could clarify leadership continuity, current elite dynamics and institutional dominance make abrupt exit unlikely. Health developments, major policy failures, or unanticipated internal realignments remain the primary low-probability factors that could still shift outcomes within the timeframe.
